Projects

OpenExo — Structural

Hip Module Design & Fabrication

MAY 2026 — PRESENT

Led design and manufacture of the hip module for OpenExo, an open-source wearable lower-limb exoskeleton — from Fusion 360 CAD through FEA validation, 3D printing, CNC machining, and final assembly, iterating through several real structural failures along the way.

CAD / Analysis
Fusion 360, FEA
Materials
PLA → Onyx → CF
Processes
FDM, CF print, CNC
Vendor
SendCutSend
  • Diagnosed a fractured PLA hip cuff and cracked cuff slider, tracing the failure to a high-stress zone at the strut interface — findings that directly shaped the reinforced carbon fiber redesign.
  • Redesigned the hip abductor from scratch after the PLA prototype, validating the new geometry with FEA before committing to final material.
  • Milled and hand-finished carbon fiber struts in the machine shop, working through drilling-speed failures (one strut cracked) and post-processing exposed fiber for safe wear.
  • Caught and corrected a 200-micron shoulder screw bore tolerance issue caused by anodizing buildup on outsourced aluminum parts — before it reached final assembly.
  • Designed custom motor mounts for both AK60-6 and AK80 actuators to validate fit against the strut assembly on a mechanical breadboard.
  • Machined and anodized the abduction bracket in 6061-T6 aluminum, the finished version of the part after resolving the SendCutSend tolerance and hole-spacing issues found in earlier iterations.
OpenExo — Actuation

Bowden Cable Transmission — Ankle Actuation

MAY 2026

Prototyped the Bowden cable transmission that lets the ankle's drive motor sit proximally on the leg instead of at the joint itself — directly cutting the distal mass a wearer has to swing with every step.

Function
Remote actuation
Insert material
TPU (flexible)
Variants tested
Tapered / Straight
Guide
Dual carbon fiber tube
  • Designed, printed, and compared two TPU cable insert geometries — tapered and straight — to evaluate cable routing smoothness and fit.
  • Assembled the full carriage: sliding rail, motor mount plate, and dual-tube guide block, iterating through early print failures to improve reliability.
  • Working with a graduate student on the broader transmission system, contributing prototype design and hands-on assembly.
Class Project — CAD Design

Military Drone Concept — Multi-Payload Quadcopter

CLASS FINAL PROJECT

Designed a fully modeled (non-functional) quadcopter concept in SolidWorks as a team final project, featuring a deployable landing leg mechanism, a 2-axis camera gimbal, and mounted payload modules including a flashlight, flare, and laser pointer.

Software
SolidWorks
Type
Design Concept (Non-Functional)
Team
Group Project
Components
26 Unique Parts
  • Modeled a full quadcopter assembly including body shell, four frame arms, motors, propellers, and a hinged multi-leg landing gear system.
  • Designed a 2-axis camera gimbal assembly (yaw-to-roll and pitch-to-roll elbow joints) to stabilize a mounted camera module.
  • Integrated deployable payload modules — a flashlight, flare, and laser pointer — each mounted via custom clamp holders on the frame.
  • Produced full engineering drawings, including an exploded-view assembly with a complete bill of materials for all 26 components.
